The '''1967–68 season''' is '''[[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid Club de Fútbol]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|65th season]] in existence and the club's [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|36th consecutive season]] in the top flight of Spanish football.

== Summary ==
The club won its 13th League title ever and second in a row<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Diario Marca|title=La flor del Real Madrid Yé-yé|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/07/07/futbol/mas_futbol/1310030818.html?a=d4b430a7096e9c1309423dd461d4cc04&t=1354897168|access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref> after recovered the number one spot from [[Atlético Madrid]] on round 16, the team clinched the trophy three points above runners-up [[FC Barcelona|CF Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/especiales/2002/02/centenario/1955.html |title=Historia del Real Madrid, 100 años uno a uno|publisher=Diario El Mundo|access-date=7 December 2019}}</ref> In the [[1967–68 Copa del Generalísimo|Copa del Generalísimo]], the team reached the [[1968 Copa del Generalísimo Final|Final]] with a chance to secure the [[Double (association football)#Spain|domestic double]]. There, Real faced Barcelona, losing 0–1 after an early Zunzunegui own goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/copa68.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111204231825/http://www.linguasport.com/futbol/nacional/copa/Copa68.htm |url-status=usurped |archive-date=4 December 2011 |title=Copa del Rey 1968|publisher=linguasport.com}}</ref> After the end of the season, President Santiago Bernabéu gave the Laureada trophy to [[Pirri]] due to his outstanding playing in favor of Real Madrid, being only one of two players in club history to receive it.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/1a_division/real_madrid/es/desarrollo/1059013.html|title=This Way Pirri Won La Laureada|work=Marca|location=Spain|accessdate=2 July 2020|date=18 November 2007|author=Ulises-Sanchez Flor}}</ref>

Meanwhile, in the [[1967–68 European Cup|European Cup]] the team suffered to win the preliminary round series against [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] with young star playmaker [[Johan Cruijff]], the Dutch squad was finally defeated after extra time in Madrid. Then, the squad clinched the round of 16, and quarterfinals against [[Sparta Praha]] reaching the semi-finals where it was defeated by young star forward [[George Best]] and his [[Manchester United]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stretfordend.co.uk/seasons/season1968.html |publisher=stretfordend.co.uk |title=Man U Season 1967–68}}</ref> losing the away match of the series (0–1 at [[Old Trafford]]). In the second leg at Madrid, the squad took a 3–1 advantage score in the first half, however, in the second half Manchester United managed to score two goals and getting the draw to reach the Final. The English squad included in its line up players such as: [[Denis Law]] (under surgery just before the Final), [[1966 FIFA World Cup]] Champion [[Bobby Charlton]] and Nobby Stiles.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/players/realmadrid-in-ec.html|title=Real Madrid CF – All the players in European Cups|publisher=[[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]]|accessdate=18 January 2020}}</ref>

Goalkeeper [[Andres Junquera]] won the [[Zamora Trophy]] with the better average of goals conceded.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rtve.es/deportes/20190506/muere-andres-junquera-exportero-del-real-madrid-gano-cinco-ligas-tres-copas/1932622.shtml|title=Fútbol {{!}} Real Madrid – Muere Andrés Junquera, exportero del Real Madrid con el que ganó cinco Ligas y tres Copas|trans-title=Football {{!}} Real Madrid – Death of Andrés Junquera, former Real Madrid goalkeeper with whom he won five Leagues and three Cups|publisher=[[RTVE]]|language=Spanish|date=6 May 2019|accessdate=9 October 2019}}</ref> After 9 years, two times European Cup winner defender [[Pachin]] left the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2021/02/10/6023e6cfca4741402d8b45cb.html|work=Marca|location=Spain|title=Legendary Real Madrid player Pachin dies|date=10 February 2021|author=Miguel Angel Garcia}}</ref>
